claim: Let \(V\subset\mathbb C^n\) be any complex realization of \(U_{r,n}\), and let \(Y_V\subset(\mathbb P^1)^n\) be its matroid Schubert variety. If \(\operatorname{ind}(Y_V)\) is the least positive integer \(m\) for which \(mK_{Y_V}\) is Cartier, then \(\operatorname{ind}(Y_V)=1\) for \(r=1\), while \(\operatorname{ind}(Y_V)=\frac{n-r+1}{\gcd(n-r+1,2)}\) for \(2\le r\le n\). In particular, the rank-two family has unbounded canonical Cartier index, although every member is \(\mathbb Q\)-Gorenstein.
scientific_limitations_and_integrity: The formula is limited to complex realizations of uniform matroids. It computes the canonical Cartier index, not singularity type. The general cocircuit criterion is prior work; the new statement is the exact least-index formula and unboundedness in rank two. No independent validation or external certification is claimed.
title: Unbounded canonical indices for uniform matroid Schubert varieties
